drip.author: RAWfiles
drip.title: First cold morning of the fall put dew on every spiderweb in the yard, and there are about forty of them I walked past all summer
drip.body:
Went out early with the camera and they were everywhere. Between the fence boards, across the gap in the hedge, one strung from the mailbox to the recycling bin.

Turns out orb weavers reach full size around now, which is why the big webs seem to show up all at once in September. A lot of them also eat their web and spin a fresh one every day, so the one I shot this morning won't be the same web tomorrow.

comments.author: verdigris
comments.body: a sculpture that gets taken down and rebuilt every day, and nobody visits the gallery unless there's dew

replies.author: RAWfiles
replies.body: and the gallery hours are about twenty minutes, until the sun burns it off

comments.author: chinook_wind
comments.body: found one of these with my face taking out the recycling last week. I wouldn't call that mildly interesting. I'd call it an ambush

comments.author: compost_mentis
comments.body: The garden spiders are the only staff I don't pay, and this is their busiest month. Every web in my tomato cage is a small act of pest control.

comments.author: GlassOnion88
comments.body: movie cobwebs are usually rubber cement blown through a spinning fan, which is exactly why they never look this good up close

drip.author: chinook_wind
drip.title: The crosswalk by my place goes cuckoo when you cross one way and chirps when you cross the other, and it's on purpose
drip.body: Cuckoo means you're crossing north-south, chirp means east-west, so someone who can't see the signal can tell which street they're about to cross. I've walked through that intersection for years and only noticed because the dog stopped to stare at the speaker.

comments.author: verdigris
comments.body: so the intersection is quietly giving directions to anyone who listens. a compass that sings

comments.author: high_park_heron
comments.body: Birder here, and I'll confess the cuckoo crosswalk has turned my head more than once. The cuckoos we actually get in Canada don't even sound like that. I knew. I turned around anyway.

replies.author: chinook_wind
replies.body: a bird person getting fooled by a speaker on a pole is the best thing I'll read all week

comments.author: RAWfiles
comments.body: I've probably got this in the background of a hundred street clips and never once noticed there were two different sounds

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: the light in our rink parking lot makes exactly one sound, a buzz, and it means nothing. I envy your crosswalk

drip.author: zamboni_dreams
drip.title: Tournament season is back, which means the game pucks are back in the rink office freezer next to someone's lunch
drip.body:
Frozen pucks bounce a lot less and slide more predictably, so for games we keep them cold and swap them out as they warm up. The pros do the same thing, just with more pucks and fewer frozen lasagnas.

There's a label on the shelf that says PUCKS, DO NOT EAT. I didn't write it. I would like to know what happened.

comments.author: GlassOnion88
comments.body: the DO NOT EAT label is doing so much storytelling. somebody has a history

replies.author: zamboni_dreams
replies.body: ten years here and nobody will tell me. I've asked. there's a lot of looking at the floor

comments.author: chinook_wind
comments.body: so the lasagna and the pucks are both technically game-day prep. I respect a multi-use freezer

comments.author: RAWfiles
comments.body: tried photographing a rec game once and half my frames were a puck mid-hop. now I know nobody was freezing them

comments.author: offsidewinger
comments.body: Beer league D-man. Nobody freezes our pucks. They live in a mesh bag in a trunk that's been through a whole summer, and they play exactly like it.

drip.author: verdigris
drip.title: The same maple on my street turns red two weeks before every other tree on the block, every single year
drip.body: It's already fully red while the rest are still green with a little yellow at the edges. It's the one planted closest to the road, in a small square of dirt with sidewalk on every side.

comments.author: solsticegrower
comments.body: That little square of dirt is probably why. Trees under stress from compacted soil, road salt or not enough water often colour up early. It's beautiful, but it's also the tree telling you it's having a hard time.

replies.author: verdigris
replies.body: so the prettiest tree on the street is the most stressed one. I'm going to go stand near it in solidarity

comments.author: chinook_wind
comments.body: we've got one like that at the edge of a grocery store parking lot. everyone stops to photograph it and it's quietly having the worst year of anyone

comments.author: RAWfiles
comments.body: every photographer on your street already knows about that tree, whether they admit it or not

comments.author: GlassOnion88
comments.body: a set designer would never let one tree get that far ahead of the others. real life has worse continuity and I love it

drip.author: GlassOnion88
drip.title: Watched an old 35mm print at a repertory screening and caught the little circles that flash in the top-right corner before a reel ends
drip.body:
Two sets. The first a few seconds before the end of the reel, the second right at the end. They were the projectionist's cue to start the next projector and switch over without the audience noticing.

I've watched hundreds of films and never saw them until someone told me where to look. Now I can't sit through an old print without waiting for them.

comments.author: cassette_futurism
comments.body: Fight Club calls them cigarette burns, which is how half the people I know learned they exist. Changeovers were a real craft, and the good projectionists were completely invisible.

comments.author: verdigris
comments.body: a secret message meant for one person in the building, flashed in front of everyone

replies.author: GlassOnion88
replies.body: and that one person was upstairs in a booth, probably eating a sandwich, waiting to hit a switch

comments.author: zamboni_dreams
comments.body: we have a version at the rink. the ice crew watches the clock, the gate guy watches the ice crew, and nobody in the stands knows the whole building is running on cues

comments.author: RAWfiles
comments.body: film still has all the best hidden rituals. digital just has a progress bar

late_comments.author: chinook_wind
late_comments.body: found this again because our local rink just put the ice back in for the season, and I stood at the glass watching the white go on like it was a gallery opening. nobody else was watching. their loss

late_comments.author: zamboni_dreams
late_comments.body: came back to this after seeing the same thing with rain across the rink parking lot this week. wet asphalt on one side, dry on the other, a line straight down the middle of the lot
